download_all_addons_efb() skipped AdnGoS whenever vendor/googlesheet/class-Emsfb-googlesheet.php existed. In runtime scope that branch is unreachable with the file present (the generic already-present guard runs first), so the change is runtime-neutral; in admin scope it made Create/Panel Recover a no-op for a pre-migration package: success false, no request, same card after reload. Proven by the googlesheet_create scenario (red without the change, green with it) and on the e2e site.

A site on the new core with the old package shows the Google Sheet screens in English (GoogleSheetAddon::tx() and googlesheet-efb.js t() carry inline English fallbacks) until Create/Panel recovery or an add-on update installs the new zip.

73 literal gettext calls with domain easy-form-builder (51 distinct msgids) remain in vendor/googlesheet/class-Emsfb-googlesheet.php (menu titles, AJAX messages, the Yes/No of the clear-log dialog); reported, not moved.

Plurals: the add-on evaluates the four _n() entries with n=1 and n=2 and googlesheet-efb.js picks one of those two for any count, so languages with more than two plural forms (ar, ary, ru_RU, pl_PL, cs_CZ) show the n=2 form for every count other than 1. Pre-existing; not changed.
fr_FR and ar approved strings for the three fragments around the service-account email differ in leading/trailing whitespace from the msgid; kept verbatim (not UI-breaking), listed as suggestions.

Human Shield reads its phrases only through efb_get_addon_phrases(humanshield): Emsfb_Human_Shield_Admin::get_i18n() re-keys hsFooBar to fooBar for the JS, Emsfb_Human_Shield::phrase() uses the raw key for REST messages. A visitor request that gets a Human Shield block message now also loads the provider file and efb-human-shield for that locale (efb_get_addon_phrases merges the provider group). The message values are unchanged.

A site on the new core with the old package sees the Security & Spam Protection panel in English (the JS carries English fallbacks) until Create/Panel recovery (only while AdnHSH is on) or an add-on update installs the new zip. The panel itself is always in the menu.

The panel is reachable while AdnHSH is off, but the C4 lock and the C6 locale refetch act only on enabled add-ons: with the add-on off, a locale whose file was pruned before the site started using it shows the panel in English until the add-on is switched on or updated.

notes: First add-on whose phrases came from the base $lang array of includes/functions.php instead of a phrase group: the provider's base() carries all 82 keys and group() is empty, and EfbAddonPhrases::get_addon_base_phrases_efb() merges base() into text_efb(1) and text_efb(2) before the page_request group merge.

The 82 entries were a contiguous, self-documented block of the $lang array (each with its own one-line /* translators: */ comment, each written $state && isset($ac->text->K) ? $ac->text->K : esc_html__(...)); all 82 moved with their comment, English, gettext function and override expression byte-for-byte, and every override key equals its array key.

82 keys, 82 unique msgids, one gettext function (esc_html__), no plurals, no contexts. One msgid carries placeholders (%1$s %2$s). Two carry HTML entities that stay entities (Message…, ...—...); negateGroup carries a literal U+2014 em dash.

Removed from core: 164 lines of includes/functions.php (82 entries + 82 comments), no additions except the manifest line. Nothing was removed from includes/phrases.php: the Autofill group keeps its own "optional" and "runTest" entries, which is what the Auto-Populate screens read (they call text_efb(1, 'Autofill'), so the group value wins over the base one). Only the base copies moved.

msgstr = msgid warnings are concentrated on "Webhook" (kept as a loanword in 17 locales) plus a handful of natural cognates (Import/Export/Icon/Optional in de, Inspector in es/pt, Role in cs). fa_IR/fa_AF keep the approved "NOT" untranslated.

fa_IR gained three translations it did not have before: logicIf, logicThen and valueOnStrippedField are missing from the locally installed easy-form-builder-fa_IR.po but approved on translate.wordpress.org, so the efb-logic pack now supplies them. No key lost a translation.

Add-on JS hardening (vendor/logic/logic/assets/admin/js/conditional-logic-efb.js, 39 lines added / 10 changed): a missing provider file used to make the builder render raw phrase keys, because _t(k) returns its own argument. Every moved key now reads through _tf(k, <msgid>) or the new OPERATOR_FALLBACKS map, so an older package shows English. Verified: 92 _tf fallbacks equal their msgid, 0 bare _t() calls left, 5 efb_var.text.K || English reads already matched.
Fixed while doing that: the JS fallback for trackingCodeLabel said "Tracking code label" while the phrase says "Confirmation code label".
The shipped vendor/logic.zip was stale before this run: its admin JS and CSS predated the committed working tree. The rebuilt zip picks the working tree up (13 -> 156 entries, 0 lost).

Pre-existing and deliberately not changed: the front-end subset lists in includes/class-Emsfb-public.php never request formEnded or submitBlocked, so those two visitor messages always show their English JS/PHP literal even on a translated site. Both stay in core; fixing them means adding the keys to a front-end list, which is a core change outside this job.

notes: The 'payment' group is shared with the Stripe add-on and PayPal is the first of the two to migrate, so only the 10 PayPal-only keys left core. The other 65 are MULTI and stay in core until Stripe is migrated.

get_addon_phrases() merges provider group() over the core group, so on a site with PayPal installed the 65 MULTI keys are served from efb-paypal. Their English is byte-identical to the core copy, so nothing visible changes; a Stripe-only site keeps reading the core copy.
No key of the payment group is visitor-facing: every one reaches only the capability-gated PayPal payments dashboard (Emsfb_paypal_payment). Hard rule 2 therefore did not move anything extra.
No DEAD keys: all 76 payment-group keys have a live reader in vendor/paypal/ or vendor/stripe/.

vendor/paypal/class-Emsfb-paypal-payment.php:211 assigns $lang = $efbFunction->text_efb( 2 ) and never uses it; the add-on reads no base $lang key in PHP. Its only base-array read is efb_var.text.payAmount in the public paypal_efb.js, which core delivers.

31 literal gettext calls inside vendor/paypal/ still use the easy-form-builder domain (mostly visitor-facing PayPal REST error messages in class-Emsfb-paypal-handler.php). Reported, not moved, per Phase 1.3.

8 of the 10 removed keys are read unguarded in class-Emsfb-paypal-payment.php (paypals, pay_suspended, pay_suspendSub, pay_reactivateSub, pay_confirmSuspend, pay_confirmReactivate, pay_start, pay_lastPayment); pay_suspendSuccess and pay_reactivateSuccess already have isset() fallbacks. A site running the new core with the pre-migration add-on package would emit undefined-index notices on the PayPal payments screen, so the rebuilt zip must be live on both download servers before the core release.

The /* translators: */ comment on paypals still says '%s = form title. Shown as the PayPal tab label for a specific form'. Both call sites pass the 'Payments' phrase, never a form title, so the comment is stale. Preserved byte-for-byte per Hard rule 6; worth correcting in a future core-i18n pass.

Two zip entries changed bytes (assets/js/paypal-payment-efb.js, assets/js/paypal_efb.js): the shipped zip predated commit 56b0227, not an edit made by this run. vendor/ git status shows no modification to either file.

2026-09-17 (stripe run, Hard rule 3 / MULTI resolution): the 65 MULTI keys and the CORE key stripes left includes/phrases.php, and get_payment_phrases() with its register_addon('payment', ...) line was removed. efb-paypal is unchanged; a site with only PayPal installed now reads all 75 keys from efb-paypal instead of reading the shared 65 from the core group.

notes: The payment group was shared by PayPal and Stripe. PayPal migrated first (2026-09-17) and kept the 65 shared keys in core as MULTI; with Stripe migrated they have no consumer left in core, so this run removed them and the group function with them. 'payment' is now the first group served by two providers and no core group function.

get_addon_phrases('payment') merges the providers in registration order, PayPal then Stripe, so Stripe wins the 65 shared keys on a site with both add-ons. Their English is byte-identical and their translations were verified identical .mo byte for .mo byte in all 46 locales, so the PayPal dashboard reads exactly as before.

The one exception is deliberate: the five German locales now carry the approved no-break-space form of "Loading…" in efb-stripe while efb-paypal still has a plain space. On a site with both add-ons the approved form wins, which is what German sites saw from the core pack before either migration. efb-paypal should get the same one-character correction in a PayPal re-run.

Every one of the 66 keys is read only by vendor/paypal/class-Emsfb-paypal-payment.php and vendor/stripe/class-Emsfb-stripe-payment.php, both through efb_get_addon_phrases('payment'). No core file, front-end subset, public REST route or visitor email reads any of them, so FRONT and CORE are empty for this run.

vendor/logic/logic/assets/admin/js/conditional-logic-efb.js names pay_completed and pay_failed in OPERATOR_LABELS, but its own comment records that the builder screens never request the payment group, so _t() returns the key and its OPERATOR_FALLBACKS supply the English words. Neither key exists in the base $lang array (checked in text_efb(1)), so that reference cannot reach the group definition and does not keep the keys in core (Hard rule 3). Removing them changes nothing there.
No DEAD keys: the Stripe dashboard reads all 66 remaining keys of the group, including pay_copy, which it reads through an isset() fallback.

vendor/stripe/class-Emsfb-stripe-payment.php:210 assigns $lang = $efbFunction->text_efb( 2 ) and never uses it, exactly like the PayPal copy; the add-on reads no base $lang key in PHP, and its admin JS reads only efb_stripe_payment.text. base() is therefore empty.

5 literal gettext calls inside vendor/stripe/ still use the easy-form-builder domain: 'Copy' (the pay_copy fallback), 'Yes', 'No', 'Download PDF' and 'PDF download ready.' at class-Emsfb-stripe-payment.php:320-324. Reported, not moved, per Phase 1.3.

The /* translators: */ comment on 'stripes' says '%s = form title. Shown as the Stripe tab label for a specific form'. Both call sites pass the translated 'Payments' phrase, never a form title, so the comment is stale. Preserved byte-for-byte per Hard rule 6, like the identical stale comment on PayPal's 'paypals'.

All 66 keys are read unguarded as $phrases['key'] in class-Emsfb-stripe-payment.php except pay_copy, so a site running the new core with the pre-migration Stripe package would emit undefined-index notices on the Stripe payments screen. The rebuilt vendor/stripe.zip must be live on both download servers before the core release, and so must vendor/paypal.zip, because the 65 shared keys left core in this run as well.

includes/phrases.php still declares the empty, unregistered get_stripe_phrases() (and get_webhook_phrases()). They predate this work, are referenced nowhere, and hold no key, so this run left them untouched; worth removing in a separate cleanup.

notes: The core 'sms' phrase group is gone: get_sms_phrases() held exactly these 25 keys, its only reader was the add-on's own dashboard (vendor/smssended/class-Emsfb-sms.php:119 calls text_efb(2,'sms')), so under the 2026-09-17 rule every key moved. EfbAddonPhrases::register_addon('sms', ...) was removed with it and register_addon_provider_efb('sms', 'smssended', ...) took its place; efb_get_addon_phrases('sms') now returns the 25 keys from the provider alone.

Three base $lang keys moved as well: waiting ('Waiting'), smscw (the 'configure the SMS sending method' error) and to ('To'). grep -rn over the whole plugin with vendor/ included found no reader outside vendor/smssended for any of them; none is in a front-end subset of includes/class-Emsfb-public.php.

waiting was written $state ? $ac->text->waiting : ... and moved as $state && isset($ac->text->waiting) ? ... (the one change Hard rule 6 allows). smscw and to already had the isset() form. Every msgid, gettext function (esc_html__ throughout), translators comment and override key is byte-identical to core; only the text domain changed.

Delivery change in the add-on (required by the ADDON rule): vendor/smssended/smsefb.php::send_sms_Emsfb() used text_efb(array('error403','somethingWentWrongPleaseRefresh','messageSent','pleaseFillInRequiredFields','smscw')). A subset request never loads add-on files, so smscw would have resolved to nothing. It now calls text_efb(2), which merges base() of every registered provider. The other four keys are unchanged core phrases and resolve exactly as before (verified byte-identical in en_US).

28 keys, 28 unique msgids, one gettext function (esc_html__), no plurals, no contexts, no placeholders. Entities preserved: typeYourMessage keeps …, smsSendMessages keeps a literal &, smsHelpNote3 keeps the escaped apostrophe in "each form's settings".

Translation sourcing: 245 of 1288 msgstr came verbatim from approved translate.wordpress.org strings (fa_IR, ar, de_DE and fr_FR are 28/28 approved; nl_NL, nl_NL_formal, nl_BE and pt_BR 27/28; sv_SE 11; ru_RU 6; tr_TR 3; de_DE_formal 3; pt_PT and da_DK 1). Spanish (all 13), Italian, Polish, Czech, Vietnamese, Indonesian, Hungarian, Japanese and all three Chinese locales have zero approved strings in this plugin's wp.org project today, so those are original work. 34 msgstr were reused from the telegram add-on ('Quick Tips'). msgstr = msgid: 0 across all 46 locales.

Reported upstream for translate.wordpress.org (kept verbatim, not changed): de_DE/de_DE_formal render 'To' as 'Bis' (= until) instead of the recipient-header 'An'; ru_RU renders it as 'для'; nl_NL/nl_NL_formal render 'Important Notes' as 'Belangrijke reacties' (reacties = replies), while nl_BE has the correct 'Belangrijke notities'; fr_FR's smsHelpNote1 lost the digit in '+1' and smsPhoneHint has a stray space after '+'; pt_BR renders 'sent' in the singular ('enviada') although the JS concatenates it after a count.

19 keys the add-on's JS reads are defined nowhere in core (secure, smsGuideLink, smsReadFullGuide, smsHelpSetup, smsGuideStep1-4, smsGuideFormConfig, smsGuideForm1-4, smsGuideCodes, smsCode*). They always show the JS English literal, on every locale, before and after this run. Listed under READ_BUT_NEVER_DEFINED; fixing them means adding phrases, not moving them.

The JS fallback literals of several keys have drifted from the phrases themselves (e.g. efb_var.text.smsHelpDesc || 'Learn how to set up SMS notifications' vs the phrase 'Learn how to use the SMS feature'; smsHelpNote4's fallback is a different sentence entirely; the waiting fallback says 'Sending…'). Only visible when a phrase is missing. Reported, unchanged.

vendor/smssended.zip did not exist locally (vendor/.gitignore ignores smssended.zip, and no build was ever committed, unlike every other add-on). The rebuilt zip was therefore diffed against the pristine tracked payload of vendor/smssended at HEAD: 4 files kept, 147 entries added (provider + languages/), 0 lost.
